name: Active Scanning
description: Adversaries probe addresses and ports for reachable services before choosing a target.
detection: A single source hitting many ports or paths in a short window; IDS scan signatures; firewall deny spikes.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
description: A malicious attachment that the user opens, usually an office document or archive.
detection: Mail gateway detonations; child processes of outlook/winword (winword -> cmd/powershell); macro-enabled docs.

name: Spearphishing Link
description: A link to a credential-harvesting page or a payload download.
detection: Proxy logs for newly registered domains; lookalike domains; clicks followed by a POST to a non-corporate host.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Exploiting a flaw in an internet-facing service — VPN, web app, mail gateway.
detection: WAF alerts; unusual POST bodies to a known CVE endpoint; web server spawning a shell; new process trees under w3wp/php-fpm.

name: External Remote Services
description: Logging in through VPN, RDP or Citrix with stolen or guessed credentials.
detection: Impossible travel; logins from hosting ASNs; first-seen device for an account; off-hours access to a service that is normally 9-5.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Using real credentials so nothing looks broken. The quietest way in.
detection: MFA fatigue; new MFA device enrolment; privilege changes shortly after login; access to resources the role never touched.

name: PowerShell
description: Scripted execution on Windows, often encoded or downloaded in memory.
detection: -enc/-EncodedCommand; DownloadString/iex; powershell spawned by office or a service; AMSI hits.

name: Windows Command Shell
description: cmd.exe used for discovery and execution.
detection: cmd /c with net, whoami, ipconfig, tasklist in quick succession; cmd spawned by a web server.

name: Unix Shell
description: Shell execution on Linux or macOS, often through a web shell.
detection: bash -c with curl|sh; reverse-shell one-liners; shell spawned by www-data or nginx.

name: Malicious File
description: The user runs the file. Everything before this is delivery.
detection: Execution from Downloads/Temp; unsigned binaries; file written by a browser then executed within minutes.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
description: Persistence that survives reboot without a service.
detection: schtasks /create; tasks pointing at user-writable paths; cron entries added outside change windows.

name: Windows Service
description: A service installed for persistence or to run a payload as SYSTEM.
detection: sc create/new service; service binary in Temp or ProgramData; 7045 events with an unsigned image.

name: Registry Run Keys
description: Autostart entries in HKCU/HKLM Run keys.
detection: Autoruns drift; new Run value pointing at AppData; identical value across many hosts.

name: Create Account
description: A new local or domain account for later use.
detection: 4720/4728 events; account created outside a joiner process; account never used but never disabled.

name: Account Manipulation
description: Adding credentials, MFA devices or group membership to an existing account.
detection: Group membership changes to privileged groups; new SSH key in authorized_keys; MFA device added.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: A local exploit to go from user to SYSTEM/root.
detection: Unexpected token elevation; kernel exploit artefacts; process integrity level jumping.

name: Bypass User Account Control
description: Getting elevated without the prompt.
detection: UAC-related registry changes; fodhelper/sdclt/computerdefaults parent processes.

name: Disable or Modify Tools
description: Turning off the defences first — AV, logging, firewall.
detection: Defender exclusions added; auditpol changes; service stopped then deleted; ETW patched.

name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
description: Deleting tools and logs after use.
detection: USN journal gaps; event log cleared (1102); mass deletion in a directory.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Encoding or packing to survive inspection.
detection: High-entropy blobs; base64 in script blocks; strings that decode to a URL; mismatched file type and content.

name: Rundll32
description: Signed Windows binaries used to run someone else's code.
detection: rundll32 with a remote or temp DLL; ordinal exports; rundll32 spawned by office.

name: Brute Force
description: Guessing passwords, spraying, or credential stuffing.
detection: Many failures per account or per IP; one password against many accounts (spraying); success right after failures.

name: LSASS Memory
description: Dumping credentials from memory.
detection: procdump/comsvcs/minidump against lsass; handle access to lsass by a non-AV process; 4656 audits.

name: Unsecured Credentials
description: Credentials left in files, history, environment or the registry.
detection: Access to .aws/credentials, .env, ~/.bash_history; grep patterns for password= in user directories.

name: Account Discovery
description: Enumerating users and groups.
detection: net user /domain, Get-ADUser, repeated 4624 logon-type-3 probes; ldapsearch against the DC.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Mapping what else is reachable from the foothold.
detection: Internal port sweeps from a workstation; nmap-like traffic east-west; many RSTs from one host.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: RDP to the next host with stolen credentials.
detection: 4624 type 10; RDP from a workstation to a workstation; unusual source subnet for RDP.

name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Copying and running via admin shares.
detection: 5140/5145 access to ADMIN$/C$; service creation after a share write; psexec-style artefacts.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web
description: C2 hidden in normal HTTP(S) traffic.
detection: Beaconing at fixed intervals with jitter; consistent small POSTs; long-lived connections to one host.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Pulling tools onto the host.
detection: certutil/curl/wget downloading to Temp; executables written by powershell; archive downloads on servers.

name: Encrypted Channel
description: Encrypting C2 so content inspection sees nothing.
detection: Non-browser TLS to a hosting provider; self-signed certs on high ports; JA3 anomalies.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Data leaving through the same channel as the commands.
detection: Upload volume per host spiking; large POST bodies; outbound traffic to an unusual ASN.

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
description: Using a legitimate service — pastebin, cloud storage, a form API.
detection: Proxy logs to paste/file-sharing categories; new OAuth consent grants; large uploads by one user.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Ransomware. At this point you are in recovery, not prevention.
detection: Mass file renames and entropy shift; shadow copy deletion; ransom note writes; backup service stopped.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Destroying backups and shadow copies so recovery costs money.
detection: vssadmin delete shadows; wbadmin delete; bcdedit recovery disabled; backup agent service stopped.

name: Service Stop
description: Stopping security and backup services before the payload.
detection: Security service stopped outside a patch window; service stop followed by mass file writes.
